name: Elenda, the Dusk Rose
oracle_text:
Lifelink
Whenever another creature dies, put a +1/+1 counter on Elenda.
When Elenda dies, create X 1/1 white Vampire creature tokens with lifelink, where X is Elenda's power.
blocked_sentences: When Elenda dies, create X 1/1 white Vampire creature tokens with lifelink, where X is Elenda's power.

needs.what: a token pool entry for a mono-white 1/1 Vampire creature token with lifelink -- id in the house style `vampire_1_1_w_lifelink`, name "Vampire", types ["Creature"], subtypes ["Vampire"], power 1, toughness 1, keywords ["lifelink"], colors ["W"], color_identity ["W"], is_token true -- added to data/cards/tokens.cards.json so `create_token` can name it
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `create_token` is validated by `validate_token_references` in src/automtg/cards/loader.py, which raises a load error for any token id that is not already a card marked `is_token`, so a card worker cannot define the token inline. The pool's nearest Vampire lifelink tokens are the wrong color: `vampire_1_1_wb_lifelink` is white AND black and `vampire_1_1_b_lifelink` is mono-black, while `vampire_1_1_b`, `vampire_1_1_bw`, `vampire_rogue_1_1_b_lifelink` and `vampire_demon_4_3_wb_flying` each miss on color, keywords, subtypes or size. Colour is not cosmetic on these tokens -- Elenda sits in a Vampire/lifegain shell where protection from black, colour-matters counts and devotion all read the token's colour -- so substituting the white-and-black one would silently print a different card. Nothing else about the sentence is missing: the `dies` trigger with `source: "self"`, the `create_token` op and the `power_had` value key already express "create a number of tokens equal to its power" exactly as Goldvein Hydra does.
